messages.author: 91bfbd91374a94c9
messages.subject: Execution failure when trying to save or collect a file
parts:
Hi SparkR developers,

I'm trying to run a R script that reads a csv file, applies a function and saves output as a file.
The script works file for a test file but fails with the following error for a bigger file (1G, ~13,000,000 lines).


Error in save(list = filteredVars, file = rc, envir = closureEnv) :

  attempting to add too many elements to raw vector

Calls: saveAsTextFile ... getJRDD -> getJRDD -> .local -> getDependencies -> save

Execution halted

I get the above error, while testing this in spark on my local machine. 
Following SPARKR-23, I did ensure that I set SPARK_MEM and JAVA_OPTS to remove Java heap space issues.

When I ran the same script on an EC2 Spark cluster, the execution was killed at the same point but didn't print out the above error stack. The spark ec2 cluster was also able to run the script on a small test file.

Code snippet from the script :

sc <- sparkR.init(master="local[*]", sparkEnvir=list(spark.executor.memory="1g", spark.driver.host="my-ip"))

summary_stats = SparkR::collect(summary_rdd) # From unpasted code and collect() executed for this RDD

vitals_rdd = SparkR::textFile(sc, "file:///src/input_vitals.csv")

summary_df = as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, summary_stats))
norm_ip = map(vitals_rdd, function(x) { Norm(x,summary_df)})
saveAsTextFile(norm_ip, "/output/normalize")





Norm <- function(x, summary_df){
  Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "C")
  parts <- strsplit(x, ",")[[1]]
  record = list("Variable.Name" = parts[5], "Value" = parts[6],  "age_groups_string" = parts[10])
  summary_values = dplyr::filter(summary_df, variable_name == toString(record$Variable.Name) & age_groups_string == toString(record$age_groups_string))
  record$Value_Normalized = (as.numeric(record$Value) - as.numeric(summary_values$medianHR)) / (0.5 * (as.numeric(summary_values$quartile3_75) - as.numeric(summary_values$quartile1_25)))
  return(record)
}




I am new to R and trying to get a POC working for our team by executing some existing R scripts in Spark. Please let me know there's a better way to make this work with SparkR or if it's possible to execute this. Looks like it's a serializing issue and would like to know if this can be resolved.

Thanks,
Sheryl

messages.author: f4108b5f63668d70
messages.subject: Re: Execution failure when trying to save or collect a file
parts:
Hi Sheryl

From a quick look at the stack trace it looks like the summary_df is being serialized as a part of the closure submitted to Spark and that this size might be too big for the serialization step being run. Could you convert summary_df to a broadcast variable and see if it helps ? The way to do that would be to run `summary_broadcast = broadcast(sc, summary_df)` and then inside the map call you can use the variable by calling `value(summary_broadcast)`

Let me know if that helps

Shivaram

All three of them have to run a task on a Spark worker. To run tasks we automatically capture variables used in the closure and serialize them. The error indicates that the closure size is too large and can't be serialized.

Just curious -- how big is summary_stat and summary_df ? You can probably run something like `object.size(summary_stat)` to find out. Can you try with a smaller summary_stat / summary_df ?

Also there might be other variables getting captured (can't say unless I can see the whole script), so you could try to see if there are any other large variables present 

Thanks
Shivaram

messages.subject: Re: Execution failure when trying to save or collect a file
parts:
Thanks for sending a detailed log and the script. Some questions / notes below:

1. From the error message what seems to be happening is that the Java process is running out of memory when trying to serialize the Spark task. From the script I see that SPARK_MEM is commented out -- Could you try this with that set ?

2. One thing I see from the script is that there are a bunch of files being read in the main environment. As I said in the previous email the getDependencies function might not be clever enough to not serialize them (for example in_vitals or in_encounter etc.).
A very hacky workaround for now would be to split this script into two -- a pre-processing script that generates summary_stats and saves it to a file and a second SparkR script that reads in the file and just calls NormalizeToAge. 

3. I am not sure I fully understand the breakdown of tasks here. Is it the case that you have a lot of data in inpu_vitals.csv and want to process the normalization in parallel ? SparkR works well when you have a split-apply-combine style application [1] and when the input data is big. Its a good idea to think about what parts of your app need to be parallelized and what parts can be run locally.

[1] http://datasaucer.blogspot.com/2014/09/r-meets-spark-logistic-regression-in-r.html

1. From the error message what seems to be happening is that the Java process is running out of memory when trying to serialize the Spark task. From the script I see that SPARK_MEM is commented out -- Could you try this with that set ?

2. One thing I see from the script is that there are a bunch of files being read in the main environment. As I said in the previous email the getDependencies function might not be clever enough to not serialize them (for example in_vitals or in_encounter etc.).
A very hacky workaround for now would be to split this script into two -- a pre-processing script that generates summary_stats and saves it to a file and a second SparkR script that reads in the file and just calls NormalizeToAge.

- Hmm, okay. Yes, the variables (in_vitals,  in_encounter ..) could be the reason behind the serializing issue. Didn't realize session variables were also being included in the serialization apart from the ones being sent to the closure. Thanks for suggesting the workaround. I will try splitting the steps into separate scripts.

3. I am not sure I fully understand the breakdown of tasks here. Is it the case that you have a lot of data in inpu_vitals.csv and want to process the normalization in parallel ? SparkR works well when you have a split-apply-combine style application [1] and when the input data is big. Its a good idea to think about what parts of your app need to be parallelized and what parts can be run locally.

- Yes, you're right. I wanted to parallelize the normalization of values in the large input file. And then next, build a feature matrix for the clustering algo. We'll certainly put in more thought about the implementation and using the split-apply-combine pattern. 
Thanks for the link and for going through the script!


Sheryl
